prompt:
Create a clean pixel-art atlas for the exact attached 2x2 source grid. Keep the atlas canvas at the same 64:35 cell aspect ratio, four equal cells, with no gutters, text, borders, labels, or extra margins. Preserve the character, original framing, hair, skin palette, sad brow shape and native pixel-cluster style.

Cell order, left to right and top to bottom:
1) LEFT OPEN: both eyes glance gently toward the viewer's left, in the same canvas direction.
2) RIGHT OPEN: both eyes glance gently toward the viewer's right, in the same canvas direction.
3) LEFT HALF: the same left gaze with the upper lids lowered over most of the irises.
4) RIGHT HALF: the same right gaze with the upper lids lowered over most of the irises.

Keep both pupils/irises aligned to each gaze together with the source-like convergence; neither eye may stay centered while the other moves. Use small compact amber-brown irises with dark centers and tiny warm highlights. Keep the sad source's narrow eye opening and natural lower-lid contour. Do not widen the eyes, add broad cream/white sclera bands, enlarge the irises, make the gaze cross-eyed, or alter the sad expression.

For both HALF cells, lower only the upper lid enough to cover the upper iris and leave a narrow visible iris/pupil, matching the supplied half-lidded source. Keep the lower lid, cheek/skin below it, brow area, hair, and outer face exactly aligned with the reference. Do not let a cheek-colored stripe replace the lid or change its shape. Keep brow silhouette locked and consistent in all four cells.

Render crisp nearest-neighbor pixel art with no smoothing, painterly blending, blur, photographic detail, or vector eyes.
